 As University of Hawaii coach Eran Ganot said, it was both beautiful and ugly.
 That’s how basketball is sometimes, and so it was Sunday as UH overcame some rough patches and rallied when it most counted in the second half to beat Texas-Arlington 71-62 in an Outrigger Rainbow Classic game.
 A turnstile gathering of 2,461 at Bankoh Arena at Stan Sheriff Center saw the Rainbow Warriors improve to 3-0 heading into tonight’s tournament finale against Portland.
 “Every game’s a championship for us,” UH guard Jaden Matingou said.
 The Pilots blasted Bethesda 153-56 in an earlier game Sunday.
 UH’s Zack Davidson scored 14 of his team-high 21 points in the second half, including six of 10 Hawaii points when it turned a 45-43 deficit into a 53-45 lead the ’Bows would keep with 7:33 left. Fellow big man Bol Dengdit had the other four points.

 “Zack was huge,” Ganot said. “I thought with 10 minutes left in the second half we started playing our brand. … And we navigated foul trouble.”
 Davidson and Dengdit both ended up with four fouls, but combined for 36 points and 11 rebounds. Tanner Cuff and Marcus Adams led Hawaii with eight boards each, as the ’Bows outrebounded the Mavericks 44-39.
 “Basketball’s easy if you just make the easy ones,” said Davidson, who made 8-of-13 shots from the floor, almost all in the low post, and 5-of-6 free throws.
 What was mostly a brickfest of a first half ended tied at 27, as Hawaii shot 29% from the floor and UTA made just six of 11 free throws.
 But it started well for UH, with a quick 7-2 lead on two Tanner Cuff buckets sandwiching a trey from Chance Trujillo. Hawaii cooled off and led 19-6 when Adams hit a 3-pointer with 8:35 left in the half.
 The Mavericks got back into it with a 10-point run that took four minutes, while the ’Bows did things like miss four shots on the same possession.
 UTA took its first lead, 27-26, when Jerimiya Smith hit a 3-pointer a minute before the break.
 Tanner Cuff made the first of two free throws to tie it with 48 seconds left.
 Ganot and Matingou both said when UH’s offense went dry it affected the other side of the court.
 “We started off really strong, but when the shots didn’t fall it affected our energy on the defensive end,” said Matingou, who scored 12 points on 5-of-14 shooting.
 Ganot was pleased with the first five minutes of the first 20, but not the rest.
 “At halftime we said (the defensive lapse) wasn’t a sign of maturity,” the coach said.
 UTA’s Tristan Hankins was game-high with 23 points and Mier Panoam added 10.
 Trujillo pitched in with 12 for UH, and Ganot noted that he contributed three key assists in the second half. Trujillo also hit all four of his free throws after intermission.
 Ganot said the coaching staff made a deal with the players, who will play their third game in four days tonight. If they get to bed early for their proper rest, the coaches will stay up late to ensure they are prepared for Portland.
